why: The typed-operation fault record (`semio.typed-operation-fault.v1`, `🧬️schema/🧯️typed-operation-fault/🔣️.json`), written once and read by two implementations: the Rust law `app::typed_operation_fault_tests` drives `TypedOperationFault::of_fault`/`encode`/`decode`, and the AJV twin (`🧪️tests/🧯️typed-operation-fault/🟦️.ts`) validates every expected record against the schema and drives the host decoder `decodeTypedOperationFaultV1`. `records` states what one `Fault` becomes: a frozen code is non-empty and at most `limits.codeBytes` UTF-8 bytes, else the record answers `limits.untypedCode`; the message is clipped to `limits.messageBytes` UTF-8 bytes on a character boundary; the encoded record fits one result page (`limits.pageBytes`). `decodes` states which byte strings are a record: only an object of exactly the schema's four members, of this schema, with a frozen code, a known origin and a bounded message; framed text (`<code>\u001f<message>`) and prose are not. `…Repeat` spells a long string as `text` repeated `count` times.

records.name: an app refusal keeps its own code, origin and message

fault.message: Run the quality check before exporting its report.

record.message: Run the quality check before exporting its report.

records.name: a framework refusal keeps its own code

fault.message: typed operation 'x' advanced 4096 publication units without moving its ladder

record.message: typed operation 'x' advanced 4096 publication units without moving its ladder

records.name: a message above the byte bound narrows on a character boundary
an empty code is no frozen code
a code above the code bound is no frozen code
a code holding the unit separator is carried as it is — a record needs no separator
the worst-case record still fits one result page

decodes.name: a typed record decodes to itself
framed text is no record
decodes.bytes: toolRun.busythe fill run is busy

decodes.name: prose is no record
decodes.bytes: retained command reducer rejected operation: remodeling.qc-report.missing Run the quality check

decodes.name: a record of another schema is no fault record
an unknown origin is no record
an empty code is no record
a missing member is no record
